beginner.summary: For developers, testers and operations engineers who need repeatable local virtual machines but have not used Vagrant before. Covers installing Vagrant with VirtualBox, the Vagrantfile and its Ruby syntax, the machine lifecycle, finding and versioning boxes in HCP Vagrant Registry, NAT, forwarded, private and public networking, synced folders, shell, file and ansible_local provisioners, SSH access, snapshots, plugins, VAGRANT_* settings and debug logs, arm64 boxes on Apple silicon, common boot and mount errors, Docker inside a guest, and a two-machine application environment capstone.
prerequisites: Uses a terminal confidently on Windows, macOS or Linux: changing directories, editing files and running commands
Knows basic Linux administration inside a VM: apt or dnf packages, systemctl, file permissions and SSH
Has a laptop with at least 16 GB RAM, 40 GB free disk, hardware virtualisation (VT-x/AMD-V) enabled in firmware and rights to install VirtualBox or VMware
outcomes: Install Vagrant with a provider and create, start, suspend, reload and destroy machines from a Vagrantfile
Choose and pin boxes from HCP Vagrant Registry and configure memory, CPUs, networking and synced folders
Provision guests repeatably with shell, file and ansible_local provisioners and recover quickly with snapshots
Diagnose the most common boot, network and synced-folder failures and deliver a two-machine environment a teammate can start with one command

advanced.summary: For platform, DevOps and infrastructure engineers who own Vagrant environments for a team or publish boxes for others. Covers building base boxes with Packer HCL templates, multi-provider and multi-architecture box artifacts, publishing to HCP Vagrant Registry, box hardening, writing command, config, provisioner and guest capability plugins in Ruby, Patroni and MongoDB HA labs, highly available kubeadm control planes, running Vagrant in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI with nested virtualisation, matrix testing of Ansible collections, network and failure-injection labs, team-scale governance, deep debugging, Apple silicon fleets and choosing alternatives, ending with a CI-tested box pipeline capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the Vagrant intermediate level or runs multi-node Vagrant labs with host-side Ansible and more than one provider
Reads and writes Ruby at a basic level and is comfortable with Packer or another image-building tool
Has access to a Linux host with KVM or a cloud VM with nested virtualisation, plus a GitHub or GitLab account for CI work
outcomes: Build, test, version and publish multi-provider, multi-architecture Vagrant boxes with Packer and HCP Vagrant Registry
Extend Vagrant with custom commands, configuration, provisioners and guest capabilities packaged as gems
Run highly available Kubernetes and database cluster labs with repeatable failure drills
Operate Vagrant in CI and across a team with pinned versions, security controls and a clear position on alternatives
